subject: AP routing considerations & payment path for Salem Health deployment
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Clara Ng <clara.ng@salemhealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — procurement constraints and next steps

Hi Clara — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed list of next steps so we can align on your AP path (PO vs card vs marketplace):

Call highlights:
- Procurement preference: default to PO issuance for third-party SaaS; card only for low-dollar pilots/exceptions.
- Required vendor onboarding items: W9, vendor contact, remit address, invoice delivery endpoint.
- Billing cadence: Net30 by default, some lines require 45–60 days (we heard Rehab Services may need net45).
- Marketplace: Procurement is open to marketplace purchases, but only if the vendor appears on the Marketplace and can provide a Marketplace invoice and the vendor/subscription is reconciled in Coupa.

Proposed next steps (we can handle the paperwork to keep things moving):
1) I’ll send the vendor setup form (W9 + vendor metadata) and a SOC2 snapshot — can you confirm the right recipient for those?
2) You confirm whether Salem will issue a PO on day one of the contract or if the initial pilot needs a card exception.
3) If PO: share any PO number format or AP contact so we can prefill fields in our billing flow. If marketplace: confirm which marketplace (AWS Marketplace or Azure) and whether there’s an already-approved vendor listing.
4) If there are extended payment terms (net45/60), let us know which BU/line items; we’ll route to finance for approval and map expected invoice timing.

I’m attaching a short vendor setup PDF and a SOC2 snapshot to accelerate the onboarding review. Ben is looped for finance/contract questions.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0123
redwoodinference.com
--
Attachment: redwood_vendor_setup_form.pdf (form, 2 pages)
Attachment: redwood_soc2-snapshot.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

From: Clara Ng <clara.ng@salemhealth.org>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@salemhealth.org>
Date: 2027-09-18T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — procurement constraints and next steps

Thanks, Tessa — useful summary. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Salem Health standard is PO-first for any multi-month SaaS. Exceptions for cards are strictly for < $5,000 pilot spend and need approval from Procurement Lead.
- We require vendor setup before the first invoice: completed vendor form + W9 + bank remit details are mandatory.
- Payment terms: Net30 for most vendors; a handful of vendor categories (e.g., capital equipment or certain consulting contracts) run Net45, but for SaaS we generally stick to Net30. Please flag any charge types that might be classified differently.
- Marketplace: we prefer AWS Marketplace when available because it simplifies billing through our cloud procurement program, but vendor must be an AWS Marketplace seller and invoices issued by AWS are required for our recon process.

Procurement contact for vendor setup: procurement@salemhealth.org (please send forms there). If you can prefill the vendor form with your tax/legal info, that will speed review.

Clara Ng
Senior Procurement Coordinator
Salem Health
--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Clara Ng <clara.ng@salemhealth.org>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — procurement constraints and next steps

Hi Clara / Tessa — looping in a couple quick options from our side so procurement has clear alternatives: 

Option A (PO path — preferred for enterprise):
- Standard Redwood invoice monthly in arrears, Net30.
- We accept PO numbers on invoices; we can ingest PO fields in our billing system to ensure correct match.
- Required onboarding items: completed vendor form, W9, remit address; typical onboarding lead time 5–7 business days once docs are in.

Option B (Marketplace / AWS):
- If Salem purchases via AWS Marketplace, billing will come from AWS and be reconciled via your marketplace program. This reduces our onboarding steps but may change how certain discounts/promotions apply.
- We can provide an AWS Marketplace listing; time to enable varies (usually 2–3 weeks to get listings configured and approved).

Option C (Card exception for pilot):
- For small pilots < $5k we can accept a card and issue receipts. This is the quickest route but will require Procurement approval.

If procurement needs a template PO or a sample invoice with PO fields, I can attach one. Also happy to set a brief call with our Finance Ops manager to walk through the vendor setup checklist.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks both — Clara, we’ll send the prefilled vendor setup package to procurement@salemhealth.org by EOD today (includes the vendor form + W9 + sample invoice with PO field).

Action plan and timeline:
- Today (EOD): Tessa sends vendor_setup_form.pdf (prefilled) + SOC2 snapshot + sample invoice.
- Procurement review: typically 3–5 business days — if accepted, vendor will be created and first PO can be issued.
- If AWS Marketplace is preferred: procurement to confirm and we’ll open the Marketplace enablement (2–3 weeks).
- Card pilot: if Salem wants to start immediately, ask Procurement for a one-time card exception approval and we’ll process a pilot invoice under $5k.

Can you confirm whether we should proceed with Vendor setup (PO path) or explore AWS Marketplace? If PO, is procurement@salemhealth.org the right recipient for the docs (per your note, Clara)?

Thanks — I’ll include a sample invoice in the packet so AP can validate PO fields.

Best,
Tessa
